simple.meaning: חֲשַׁל (chăshal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to weaken , i.e. crush.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:40. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲשַׁל (H2827) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חֲשַׁל (chăshal) / H2827 is traced through Daniel 2:40 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2827. chashal [ חֲשַׁל ] verb shatter by a blow (Assyrian —ašâlu , shatter , perhaps thresh ; Late Hebrew חָשַׁל Pi`el shatter: Jewish-Aramaic חֲשַׁל forge, hammer , Syriac forge, furbish ; Buhl 14 compare חוּשְׁלָא ᵑ7 barkley-groats (as pounded, beaten ), and perhaps Assyrian —ûlu , barley ; Nö M 135 compare Arabic thrust, drive away (Frey), נַחְשׁוֺל ᵑ7 storm (y sea ; compare in English beaten, buffetted by waves; Assyrian loan-word Ba ZA ii. 117 ), Syriac id. ); — Pe`al Participle active חָשֵׁל Dan 2:40 (accusative of thing).
